_about: G-code, M-code and macro reference per control. Every row names its source(s) with the section or page. Meanings are BenchMate's own short wording, never copied text. A row is shown as confirmed when the maker's (or machine builder's) public document prints it, or when two independent public sources agree. Built by scripts/build_refdata.py into data/refdata.json (key gcodes).

NIST.publisher: NIST (T. R. Kramer, F. M. Proctor, E. Messina)
NIST.title: The NIST RS274NGC Interpreter - Version 3, NISTIR 6556
NIST.note: US Government work, public domain. Table 4 (modal groups, section 3.4, p. 20), Table 5 (G codes, p. 22), section 3.6 (M codes, pp. 38-39). RS274NGC is the NIST/NGC form of RS-274, the US basis of ISO 6983.

LCNC_OV.title: G-code overview, section 13 Modal Groups (tables 5 and 6)
LCNC_OV.note: GPL documentation of an RS274NGC-derived interpreter. Used as a second public source for the generic base only; LinuxCNC's own extensions are not listed as generic codes.

LCNC_M.note: Also states that M98/M99 give Fanuc-style main and sub-programs.

generic.name: Generic ISO 6983 / RS-274 (NIST RS274NGC)
generic.note: The common core every RS-274 / ISO 6983 style control is built on, as written down in the public NIST RS274NGC report. NIST wrote it for a 3-axis machining centre, so it is listed as mill only; lathes use a maker dialect. ISO 6983-1:2009 (Automation systems and integration, numerical control of machines, program format and definitions of address words, part 1) is cited by name only: its text is not public and nothing from it is copied.

fanuc.name: Fanuc (0i-F / 0i-F Plus; 30i family)
fanuc.note: Machining centre codes are from the 0i-F Plus manual; lathe codes from the 0i-F lathe manual, which has G-code systems A, B and C (chosen by parameter 3401 bits GSB and GSC). Many functions are options and the machine builder decides which are fitted; M codes other than program control are set by the builder.

haas.name: Haas (NGC mill and lathe)
haas.note: Mill codes from the current Haas online operator's manual (G codes) and the 2015 mill programming workbook (M codes). Lathe codes from the Haas Factory Outlet lathe manual (12/2024) with the 2002 Haas lathe card as a cross-check. Options are marked. Macro system variables are from the 2010 mill operator's manual (the control before the Next Generation Control).

mitsubishi.name: Mitsubishi M70 / M80 / M800
mitsubishi.note: Lathe codes from the M700L/M70L programming manual; basic codes for both lathe and machining centre from Mitsubishi's 2020 training texts. Mitsubishi offers several G-code lists selected by parameter (some functions move to other numbers); check which list your machine is set to. The M80/M800 programming manuals (IB-1501275 to IB-1501278) could not be read here, so M80/M800-only functions are not listed.

meldas.name: Mitsubishi MELDAS 60/60S (legacy lathe)
meldas.note: Older Mitsubishi lathe control. The MELDAS 600 series manual was not found in public; the 60/60S lathe programming manual is used instead. Six G-code lists (2 to 7): a code shown under 'other lists' is the same function under another list.

siemens.name: Siemens SINUMERIK 840D sl (native)
siemens.note: Siemens native (G290) programming. Siemens adds many named commands (TRANS, ROT, CYCLE81 ...) that are not G codes; only the G and M codes in Siemens's G/M handbook are listed. M functions are machine-builder specific.

siemens-iso.name: Siemens SINUMERIK 840D sl (ISO mode, milling)
siemens-iso.note: ISO dialect mode, switched on with G291 and off with G290. From the ISO Milling manual 06/2009. The ISO turning dialect was not read: lathe use is a gap.

heidenhain.name: Heidenhain TNC (DIN/ISO programs)
heidenhain.note: DIN/ISO programming on TNC milling controls, not Klartext conversational. Heidenhain numbers its cycles G200 and up and uses G-numbers that mean different things on Fanuc-style controls (G10-G16 are polar moves, G99 defines a tool). Only one page of the overview table could be read.

okuma.name: Okuma OSP (lathe, P200L/P20L)
okuma.note: OSP lathe codes confirmed from the OSP-P200L/P20L programming manual (sections 1 to 5) and Okuma's own blog. Okuma's G and M numbers differ widely from Fanuc's (LAP cycles, M codes for tailstock and chuck barriers). Okuma mill (OSP-P200M) codes are a gap.

mazak.name: Mazak (EIA/ISO, turning)
mazak.note: EIA/ISO programs only, not Mazatrol. From the Mazak turning EIA/ISO manual (2002). Code shown is standard EIA/ISO mode, series A; series B and C and the T32-compatible mode use other codes for some functions (given in the notes). Mazak machining centre EIA codes are a gap. M codes are from the INTEGREX e series programming manual (2017), a multi-tasking machine: other Mazak machines can differ.

doosan.name: Doosan / DN Solutions (HP5100 machining centre, M codes)
doosan.note: M codes only, from the builder's maintenance manual for the HP5100 horizontal machining centre. The machine builder assigns most M codes, so another Doosan model can differ: check the list in the machine's own manual. The G codes are those of the machine's NC control, which the pages read do not name.

macro.text: #0 is always empty (null) and cannot be assigned.
#1 to #33 are local variables: a macro call's arguments land here, and they are cleared when the macro or program ends.
Common variables are shared between programs; the ranges depend on the control and builder (see the disagreement note).
#1000 and up are system variables: interface signals, offsets, positions, modal state, alarms and clocks. Numbers depend on the control model, so check its manual.
Arithmetic + - * /. Functions include SIN, COS, TAN (degrees), SQRT, ABS, FIX (round down) and ROUND.
Comparisons EQ, NE, GT, GE, LT, LE. Logic AND, OR.
IF [condition] GOTO n jumps to block Nn when the condition is true. IF [condition] THEN statement runs one statement.
WHILE [condition] DO m ... END m repeats while true; loops can be nested up to 3 deep (DO1 to DO3).
G65 P<program> <arguments> calls a macro once; the macro ends with M99. G66 calls it modally, G67 cancels.
Writing to #3000 raises an operator alarm; #3006 is used for an operator message (sources differ on whether it stops: see disagreements).
Macros are an option: in this document the control needs the macro option enabled (parameter 57 bit 22, ENABLE MACRO). With it off, macro statements are treated as comments.
#1 to #33 are local, cleared at program end; G65 arguments map to them (A #1, B #2, C #3 ... X #24, Z #26).

Global variables #100-#199, #500-#699 and #800-#999 keep their values through power-off. #100-#199 and #500-#599 are reserved for Haas functions (probing, pallet changer); use #600-#699 and #800-#999.
System variables read or change offsets, inputs and outputs, parameters and settings; some are read-only. Numbers are in the operator's manual.
Assignment #100=21; arithmetic and functions such as SQRT[9]; square brackets set the order (#100=[3*[9+3]] gives 36).
Comparisons EQ, NE, GT, LT, GE, LE.
GOTOnn jumps to Nnn. IF [condition] GOTOnn jumps when true. M99 Pnn jumps to Nnn.
WH [condition] DO1 ... END1 repeats while true (as printed by Haas: WH, not WHILE).
M97 Pnn calls a local subroutine at Nnn; M98 Pnnnn calls program Onnnn; G65 Pnnnn with arguments calls a macro.
G103 P1 limits look-ahead to one block so a macro reads values at the right time (default look-ahead 80 blocks); G103 alone cancels.
A G or M code can be aliased to programs O9000-O9019 through parameters 81-100.
G65 user macro call; G66 and G66.1 modal calls (types A and B); G67 cancels.
Variables are written #n and can be used in arithmetic in a block (the manual's examples add, subtract, multiply and divide #111 to #117).
G65 user macro call; G66 and G66.1 modal calls (types A and B); G67 cancels.
R parameters are an array of REAL values written R10 or R[10]; R[<expression>] takes a computed index. How many there are is set by machine data MD28050 $MN_MM_NUM_R_PARAM.
DEF defines named variables: local (LUD), program-global (PUD) or global (GUD); types INT, REAL, BOOL, CHAR, STRING[n], AXIS, FRAME; arrays of 1 to 3 dimensions. Names up to 31 characters.
Jump instructions GOTOF (search forward), GOTOB (search back), GOTO and GOTOC, to a label or block number.
IF ... ELSE ... ENDIF; LOOP ... ENDLOOP; FOR ... TO ... ENDFOR; WHILE ... ENDWHILE; REPEAT ... UNTIL.
Comparisons use == (equal), as in IF R1==0.
In ISO dialect mode G65 calls a macro and G66 / G67 call and cancel a modal macro.
Q-parameter if-then decisions use IF with EQU (equal), NE (not equal), GT (greater than), LT (less than) and GOTO a label.
Common variables are VC numbers (for example VC1) kept in a table; local variables are temporary and cleared at the end of the program; system variables give offsets, positions, time and date.
IF [condition] N<label> jumps to the block with that sequence name when true, e.g. IF[VTLCN EQ 1] NSKIP.
Logic AND, OR, EOR (exclusive or); functions include SIN, COS, ROUND and FIX.
G65 macro program call; G66 modal call; G67 cancel.

disagreements.text: The 0i-F lathe manual (B-64604EN-1/01) lists G35 and G36 as circular threading clockwise and counter-clockwise. A third-party A/B/C table (mfgrobots) lists G36 and G37 as automatic tool compensation in X and Z. Both functions exist on Fanuc lathes; which number does which depends on the model and parameters. Check your manual.

disagreements.topic: Selecting G-code system A, B or C
disagreements.text: The maker's lathe manual says the system is chosen with bits 6 (GSB) and 7 (GSC) of parameter 3401. A third-party article says bit 0 of parameter 3401 (0 = A, 1 = B). BenchMate follows the maker's manual.

Tornos says writing #3000 raises an alarm that stops the program and #3006 shows a message without stopping. CNCCookbook says #3000 shows a message (alarm) and #3006 also stops the program. Test on your control before relying on either. cncmacrosimulator.com calls #3006 an operator message and does not say whether it stops. On the older Haas control #3006 stops like M00 (see the Haas list).

CNCCookbook gives #100-#199 (cleared at power-off) and #500-#999 (kept at power-off). Tornos, for its FANUC-controlled machines, gives #150-#199 per channel and #600-#699 shared. Ranges depend on the control model, options and machine builder.
The 2015 mill programming workbook lists G87 (bore, manual retract) and G88 (bore, dwell, manual retract). The current online operator's manual summary table does not list them.
The 2002 Haas lathe card gives tailstock chuck clamp / unclamp; the 2024 Haas Factory Outlet manual gives secondary spindle chuck clamp / unclamp.

Two third-party Okuma lathe lists share the same text. One prints G95 as 'feed per minute (mm/rev)', the other as feed per revolution. The maker's manual describes G94 and G95 as feed per minute and per revolution.

The third-party Okuma lathe lists give M98 / M99 as tailstock spindle thrust low / high, not subprogram call and return. The maker's section 5 text that was readable stops before M98, so this is not confirmed; it is a reminder not to assume Fanuc meanings on an Okuma.
The Haas macro document says #100-#199 and #500-#600 are reserved for Haas (probing, pallet changer) and #600-#699 and #800-#999 are for the user; #600 appears in both ranges as printed.

disagreements.topic: Macro variable number for one tool offset
disagreements.text: Both sources put length wear in the #10000 block, length geometry in the #11000 block, radius wear in the #12000 block and radius geometry in the #13000 block. cncmacrosimulator.com prints the ranges as #10001 to #10400 and so on, which makes offset 200 number #11200. CNCCookbook's example for offset 200 gives #11201 (and #2400 in the older numbering, which fits a block that starts at #2201). The number of the first offset depends on the control and its offset memory, so read one known offset back before a macro writes to any.

generic: LinuxCNC-only extensions (G33, G76, G7/G8, M61-M73 and others) are not listed as generic codes.
RS274NGC parameters (#1-#5400) and expressions: not yet transcribed.
fanuc: Lathe G98/G99 (feed per minute / per revolution in system A) and G94/G95 in B/C: only one third-party table; not confirmed.
Lathe G83-G89 drilling cycles: not in the readable part of the maker's table.
Lathe single-cycle codes for systems B and C (G77/G78/G79, G20/G21/G24): one third-party table only.
Grinding-only codes in the 0i-F Plus list (G75, G77-G79, G160/G161) are left out.

Fanuc's own M-code chapter and its custom macro chapter (the maker's table of system variables) are in a part of the manual that could not be read. M00, M01, M02 and M30 have one Fanuc-specific source (TIE): see the generic base. Builders' M-code lists read so far: Doosan, DMG MORI (Mori Seiki) and Mazak.

System variables marked "one source" have one independent source and no maker document. Not listed at all: interface signals (#1000 and up), #3002 to #3004 and the lathe tool offset blocks, whose numbers depend on the offset memory.
haas: Mill M-codes are from the 2015 workbook: the current online M-code page could not be read.
Haas codes only in the 2024 lathe manual and not on the 2002 card are listed from that one Haas-network source.

System variables are from the 2010 mill manual. The Next Generation Control adds and renumbers variables (its manual lists a second, newer number for many): that table could not be read. Lathe system variables: not read.
The #3004 bit table and the G-code group numbers behind #4001 to #4021 could not be read cleanly.
mitsubishi: M80/M800 programming manuals (IB-1501275 to IB-1501278) could not be read; mill G codes beyond the training text's basics are a gap.
Which G-code list (Fanuc A/B/C style) uses which code: the M70L table could not be read cleanly.
User macro variable ranges and control commands (IF, GOTO, WHILE): not confirmed.
meldas: MELDAS 600 series (600L/600M): no public manual found.
MELDAS machining centre codes: not read.
siemens: Native milling/turning cycles (CYCLE81 and so on) and frames (TRANS, ROT, SCALE, MIRROR) are commands, not G codes, and are not listed.
Siemens arithmetic functions and the full operator list: section 1.3/1.4 of the Job Planning manual could not be read.
siemens-iso: M codes in ISO mode: not read (the native M list applies to most builders).
heidenhain: Remaining pages of the DIN/ISO overview (pocket and contour cycles, coordinate transformations, M functions) could not be read.
Q-parameter ranges (Q, QL, QR, QS) and the D-function numbers (D00-D19): one independent source only (ICAM).
okuma: Okuma G90/G91, LAP cycles (G80-G88), threading cycles (G31-G33, G71-G72) and M08/M09: third-party lists only (which copy each other).
CALL / RTS / MODIN subprogram syntax: one independent source only (ICAM).
mazak: Rows marked unclear in the extraction (polar interpolation G12.1/G13.1 in standard mode, G36/G37 measuring, G52/G53 in T32 mode) are left out.

Mazak M codes are from one machine family (INTEGREX e). Left out because the reading was not clear: M163, M173, M174, M562, M563, M614 and the waiting codes M950 to M997. M codes of Mazak machining centres and plain lathes: not read.
Mazak macro system variables: not read.
doosan: Doosan lathe (Puma, Lynx) M codes: no builder list could be read.
Left out of the HP5100 list: codes printed as reserved (M20, M21, M22, M36, M37) and the external M codes (M91 to M94, M155 to M158).
dmg: Mori Seiki NL M codes whose heading could not be read the same way twice: M04, M13, M14, M34 to M36, M51, M52, M59, M70, M99, M203, M251, M252, M259, M458, M459, M482.
DMG MORI machining centres, and machines with Siemens or Heidenhain controls: not read.
